Yes, if he needs me, I helped him.

Tanvi said that she was cold.

options: The road was as slippery as a sheet of ice.
The road was as slippery than a sheet of ice.

questions.rule: Positive degree: as + plain adjective + as: as slippery as.

options: The woman waited at the crossing, felt very nervous.

chat: How was the weather in Manali?

questions.rule: To make a comparative stronger, use much: much colder. Not 'more colder' or 'very colder'.

The boy told the woman that he would help her across.
The boy said the woman that he would help her across.
questions.rule: 'said to' becomes told; 'I' becomes he, 'you' becomes her, and 'will' becomes would.

options: Sameer was stronger than any boy in the group.
Sameer was more stronger than any other boy in the group.
Sameer was stronger than any other boy in the group.
questions.rule: Sameer is in the group, so he is compared with any other boy. Do not use 'more' with '-er'.

options: If the boy had not helped her, she might have slipped on the ice.

If the boy had not helped her, she might slipped on the ice.

The teacher advised us to help those who are in need.
